sentences.text:
Shri Vijay Sundaram - Public Prosecutor for the applicant
 Shri Kapil Singhal - Advocate for respondent.
Shri Murari Lal Yadav - Advocate for the complainant.

Order 
The applicant/State has preferred this application under Section 439(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure (in short "CrPC") for cancellation of bail granted to the respondent/accused vide order dated 31.01.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.2684/2023 in relation to Crime No.146/2022 registered at Police Station Malanpur, District Bhind for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC, Sections 3/4, 5(i)/6 of POCSO Act and Sections 66-E, 67 and 67-A of I.T. Act.

2. Learned counsel for the applicant/State submits that respondent/accused has been enlarged on bail vide order dated 31.01.2023 and after releasing on bail, he has committed another offence bearing Crime No.247/23 for offence under Sections 327, 323, 294, 506, 341 of IPC.
He is having criminal record of five cases.

He has violated the terms and conditions of the bail bond, therefore,
the bail order passed in favour of the respondent/accused may be recalled and he should be taken into custody.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent/accused opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by submitting that while passing the earlier bail order, this Court has not imposed any such condition.

Subsequent offence registered against the respondent is not similar to the earlier offence registered against him, therefore, he has not violated any terms and conditions of the bail The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Arjun on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4597948/
1 bond.

sentences.text: He placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Himanshu Sharma vs. State of M.P. (SLP Criminal No.786/2024) decided on 20.2.2024.

entities.text: Himanshu Sharma vs. State of M.P. (SLP Criminal No.786/2024)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also taking note of the fact that while passing the earlier bail order, this Court has imposed only one condition that the respondent/accused will present before the Trial Court on each and every date and except this condition, no such condition has been imposed by this Court, therefore, registration of subsequent offence cannot be treated as a breach of condition of the bail bond, therefore, there is no violation of the terms and conditions of the bail bond, hence, no ground for cancellation of bail is made out.
6. Accordingly, this application for cancellation of bail is hereby rejected.
